top.line: Fractal Semantic Graph names graphs of graphs of graphs
top.para: After six months calling it "graphs of graphs of graphs", I named it Fractal Semantic Graph, defined it and published evidence. Seven live graphs, from the text of a law down to a threat in one line of code, were built with one method. This is the canonical copy of the introduction.

s0.line: Fractal means every node opens its own world
s0.para: A graph is nodes and edges; a semantic graph gives edges verbs with named inverses; an ontology is the agreed vocabulary. Fractal adds that zooming into any node opens a new world with its own types and verbs, like a regulation into articles into terms. No top, no bottom, only altitude.

s1.line: It is fractal only if a link crosses ontologies
s1.para: A risk register is a rich semantic graph but not fractal, since it stays in one vocabulary. Fractal means a link jumps worlds: from the register to security operations, to the DNS estate, to a single TCP packet. Four ontologies, one path of named edges, no adapter, because each world shares the grammar.

s2.line: Every file format is already a graph, unnamed
s2.para: Regulations, PDFs, spreadsheets, codebases and JSON are already graphs; they only need named edges. Then a question crosses formats in one traversal, a superseded node shows what was built on it, the smallest node is what the question needs, each world keeps its vocabulary, and provenance reaches the byte.

s3.line: Five grammar rules, and relates_to is banned outright
s3.para: Each altitude has its own schema but shares five rules: verbs in both directions with real inverses, relates_to banned, properties carry data not meaning, supersede never delete, render answers not whole graphs. An edge without a verb constrains nothing, and the verb's granularity sets the precision of later questions.

s4.line: Joining two graphs found eight amended articles neither knew
s4.para: Eleven altitudes run from law to compute instance: the EU AI Act graph has 1,523 nodes, AIUC-1 has 53 controls and 11,610 edges. Of 1,126 text crosswalks, 62 resolved, showing 8 of 27 articles had since been amended. A threat model traces one SQL injection to revenue, and GDPR Article 45 shows meaning flipping.

s5.line: Several altitudes are still modelled; gaps are named
s5.para: The threat model's bottom four altitudes are authored, not imported from a CMDB or cloud account. No graph yet joins enterprise architecture to obligations. Crosswalks resolve only at article level, six of the GDPR atlas's 227 edges use the banned verb, and the agent altitude has 23 primitives but no real permission import.

s6.line: Cheap edge naming, acting agents and lost schema wars
s6.para: Three changes make it practical: a language model now proposes verbs faster than humans type, so the bottleneck is purpose. Agents act on the world, so claims must trace to their source byte. And nobody won the schema wars, so the only surviving model lets everyone connect without conforming.

s7.line: Every graph is live with published read-only keys
s7.para: All the graphs can be opened, with read keys published on purpose that cannot write, walking down from the law or up from compute. Links go to sgit.ai/demos/fractal-graphs, the VoiceDebrief vault, graphs.sgit.ai and its llms.txt grammar, standards.sgit.ai and abp.sgit.ai. The article is licensed CC BY 4.0.
